'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|War in Afghanistan]]
**[[Taliban insurgency]]
***[[2021 Taliban offensive]]
****The [[Taliban]] say that they do not want to take their "fight in the mountains and deserts to infighting in cities" but warn against failed attempts at negotiations as the group advances in the country. The Taliban also condemns [[Turkey]] for sending protection to [[Kabul]]'s [[Hamid Karzai International Airport]] as part of a "violation of sovereignty" which they labeled as "reprehensible". [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/7/13/taliban-afghanistan-cities-leader-fighting (Al Jazeera)]
*[[2021 South African unrest]]
**The death toll from the protests following the arrest of former [[President of South Africa|President]] [[Jacob Zuma]] increases to 72, as more violent incidents occur. Ten of the victims died during a stampede in [[Soweto]], while others died during lootings, shootings and explosions. More than 1,000 people have been arrested. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-57818215 (BBC News)] [https://www.miamiherald.com/news/article252747538.html (''The Miami Herald'')]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[France]]'s ''[[Autorité de la concurrence]]'' fines [[Google]] a record [[Euro|€]]500M ([[USD|$]]593M) for breaching an April 2020 ruling that ordered the company to negotiate "in good faith" licensing deals with publishers and news agencies for any re-use of [[copyright]]ed content. The fine amounts to about 1.1% of the company's yearly profits. [https://www.nbcnews.com/tech/tech-news/google-hit-record-593m-fine-france-news-copyright-battle-rcna1394 (NBC News)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Uttar Pradesh]]
*****The [[States and union territories of India|Indian state]] of [[Uttar Pradesh]] reports two new cases of the [[SARS-CoV-2 lineage B.1.617|Lineage B.1.617]] [[SARS-CoV-2 Kappa variant|Kappa variant]]. [https://www.siasat.com/two-cases-of-kappa-variant-detected-in-up-all-you-need-to-know-2163680/ (''The Siasat Daily'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia]]
****[[Indonesia]] reports a record for the second consecutive day of 47,899 new cases of [[COVID-19]], thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 2.6 million. [https://news.detik.com/berita/d-5641995/pecah-rekor-lagi-kasus-corona-ri-13-juli-tambah-hampir-48-ribu?tag_from=wp_nhl_9 (detikNews)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia]]
****[[Malaysia]] reports a record 11,079 new cases and 125 deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 855,949 and the nationwide death toll to 6,385. [https://www.freemalaysiatoday.com/category/nation/2021/07/13/record-high-covid-19-cases-as-infections-breach-11000-mark/ (''Free Malaysia Today'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Cyprus]]
****[[Cyprus]] reports a record for the second consecutive day of 1,081 new cases of [[COVID-19]], thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 86,185. [https://www.financialmirror.com/2021/07/13/covid19-record-1081-new-cases-2-deaths/ (Financial Mirror)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in France]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in France]]
****[[France]] reports a new single-day record of the 1.3 million [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] appointments as the [[Government of France|Government]] pressures people to get vaccinated. [http://globalnews.ca/news/8023340/france-vaccine-appointment-record-macron/ (Global News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]
****[[Russia]] reports a record 780 deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 144,492. [https://www.rferl.org/a/russia-record-covid-deaths/31356144.html (RFE/RL)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malta]]
****[[Malta]] abandons a plan to close its border to unvaccinated travellers. Instead, they impose a mandatory quarantine. The new policy follows criticism from the [[European Commission]] that they are discriminatory. [https://timesofmalta.com/articles/view/malta-expected-to-ease-ban-on-unvaccinated-travellers-impose.886429 (''Times of Malta'')] 
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Spain]]
****[[Spain]] surpasses four million cases of COVID-19. [https://www.euronews.com/2021/07/13/us-health-coronavirus-spain (Euronews)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in El Salvador]]
***The [[Legislative Assembly of El Salvador]] suspends all public and private gatherings of large groups of people and enforces [[Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic|mandatory mask wearing]] for the next 90 days amid an increase in the number of COVID-19 cases in the [[El Salvador|country]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/el-salvador-restricts-large-gatherings-amid-rise-covid-19-cases-2021-07-13/ (Reuters)]  

'''International relations'''
*[[United States–Venezuela relations]], [[Venezuelan presidential crisis]]
**The [[United States]] [[United States Department of State|Department of State]] "strongly condemns" the arrest of opposition politician [[Freddy Guevara]] yesterday in [[Caracas]]. Guevara is a close ally of disputed president and opposition leader [[Juan Guaidó]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/us-condemns-detention-venezuelan-opposition-politician-2021-07-13/ (Reuters)]
*[[Cuba–United States relations|United States–Cuba relations]], [[United States involvement in regime change in Latin America]]
**[[List of mayors of Miami|Miami Mayor]] [[Francis Suarez]] urges the United States to consider [[air strikes]] on [[Cuba]]. Additionally, Cuban exile leaders such as [[Cuban Democratic Directorate]] spokesperson [[Orlando Gutierrez-Boronat]] calls for the [[Presidency of Joe Biden|Biden administration]] to [[United States involvement in regime change|intervene]] in the country. [https://www.wlrn.org/news/2021-07-13/call-for-u-s-military-intervention-amid-cuba-protests-sparks-miami-exile-debate (WLRN-TV)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Canadian Indian residential school gravesites]], [[Canadian Indian residential school system]]
**Members of the Penelakut Tribe in south-western [[British Columbia]] announce the discovery of at least 160 [[mass graves|"undocumented and unmarked graves"]] close to [[Kuper Island Indian Residential School]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2021/jul/13/canada-unmarked-graves-british-columbia-residential-school (''The Guardian'')] [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/7/13/more-unmarked-residential-school-graves-discovered-in-canada (Al Jazeera)]
'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2021 Cuban protests]]
**In [[Miami]], protesters temporarily block the [[Florida State Road 826|Palmetto Expressway]] in both directions in order to show support for Cuban protestors. [https://www.miamiherald.com/news/local/community/miami-dade/west-miami-dade/article252756578.html (''Miami Herald'')]
**The [[San Isidro Movement]] says that over 100 people have been arrested since protests began in Cuba. [[Spaniards|Spanish]] [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Spain)|Minister of Foreign Affairs, European Union and Cooperation]] [[José Manuel Albares]] also calls for the release of Cuban journalist Camila Acosta. [https://keyt.com/news/national-world/cnn-other/2021/07/13/more-than-100-arrested-or-missing-in-cuba-after-widespread-protests-say-activists/ (KEYT-TV)] [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2021/jul/13/cuba-protests-activists-journalists-protesters-detained (''The Guardian'')]
**Cuban [[YouTube|YouTuber]] Dina Fernandez, also known as Dina Stars, says that she was detained by Cuban security forces in [[Havana]] during an interview. [https://cnnespanol.cnn.com/2021/07/13/youtuber-cubana-dina-stars-denuncia-detencion-durante-entrevista-en-vivo/ (CNN en Español)]
*[[2021 Samoan constitutional crisis]]
**[[Naomi Mataʻafa]] accuses [[Tuila'epa Sa'ilele Malielegaoi]] of a desperate "attack on the rule of law" and calls on him to recognize defeat in the past election. Several Pacific Island nations such as the [[Federated States of Micronesia]], [[Palau]] and the [[Marshall Islands]] have recognized Mataʻafa as the new Prime Minister of Samoa. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/446826/samoa-s-tuilaepa-accused-of-desperate-attack-on-rule-of-law (RNZ)]
